record.paper_title: Some open problems in control theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on a bounded smooth domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$):
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \nu\Delta u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0, \qquad \text{in } (0,T)\times\Omega,$$
with prescribed initial datum $u(0,\cdot)=u_0$ in a suitable function space (e.g.\ $L^2_{\mathrm{div}}(\Omega)$ or $H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\Omega)$), and with the no-slip boundary condition $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, where $\Gamma\subset\partial\Omega$ is a fixed nonempty open subset of the boundary on which one is allowed to prescribe a boundary control $u|_{(0,T)\times\Gamma}=g$ (with $g$ chosen in an appropriate trace space and consistent with incompressibility).

Question: Is the Navier–Stokes system controllable in the following sense? For every $T>0$, every initial state $u_0$, and every target state $u_1$ (in the chosen function space), does there exist a boundary control $g$ on $(0,T)\times\Gamma$ such that the corresponding solution satisfies $u(T,\cdot)=u_1$? Equivalently, decide global exact (or null) controllability of the Navier–Stokes equations under the no-slip boundary condition outside the control region.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: local exact controllability is known, and small-time global exact controllability has been established by Coron, Marbach, and Sueur for Navier slip-with-friction boundary conditions (and extensions to curved boundaries). However, the global exact (or null) controllability of the Navier–Stokes equations under the classical no-slip boundary condition on the uncontrolled part of the boundary remains an open problem (a question originally posed by J.-L. Lions).

status_evidence.title: Small-time global exact controllability of the Navier-Stokes equation with Navier slip-with-friction boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Coron, Marbach, Sueur prove small-time global exact controllability under Navier slip-with-friction boundary conditions; the no-slip case is highlighted as open.
status_evidence.claim: Global exact controllability with Navier slip BC is established; the no-slip case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Controllability of the Navier–Stokes Equation in a Rectangle with a Little Help of a Distributed Phantom Force
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses global controllability with no-slip conditions using a small distributed force, indicating the pure boundary no-slip case is still open.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the no-slip boundary controllability question remains open without auxiliary forces.

status_evidence.title: Global Controllability of the Navier-Stokes Equations in the Presence of Curved Boundary with No-Slip Conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent partial results extending controllability under no-slip conditions in special geometries.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on no-slip global controllability in special settings.
